In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the fatigue hystereses loops models of unidirectional composites are derived based on the fiber slipping relative to the matrix upon unloading and reloading.
the fatigue damage mechanism is fiber/matrix interface debonding and sliding, and the tension-tension life of C/SiC at room temperature and elevated temperatures is dominated by interface debonding.

the tension-tension cyclic loading at room temperature and high temperature in air atmosphere is a very effective way to degrade the fibers and the interface shear stress, and the tension-tension S-N curves at room temperature and at 800 °C are in good agreement with the experimental data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fatigue life of unidirectional ceramic-matrix composite is mainly determined by the interface shear stress and fibers strength degradation.

the fatigue hystereses loops models for different fiber/matrix interface slip cases have provided a theoretical basis for estimating fiber/matrix interface debonding shear stress and fiber strength degradation.

the fiber slipping in the debonded region is the primary damage mechanism for tension-tension fatigue failure of unidirectional ceramic-matrix composites, and the tension-tension cyclic loading can cause the fiber strength and interface shear strength degradation, and the fiber failure is the dominant damage mechanism for tensiontension fatigue failure of C/SiC composites.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the tension-tension hysteresis loop model can be used to estimate the fiber/matrix interface debonding and slipping in the interface debonds region, which can be further used to estimate fatigue life of unidirectional ceramic-matrix composite.
it is possible to predict the tension-tension cyclic fatigue life of C/SiC composites based on the fatigue hystereses loops and fibers failure model.
the fatigue hystereses loops model for different interface slip conditions can be used for fatigue damage assessment of unidirectional ceramic-matrix composites.
